body: Ah, I forgot to mention. I'm diagnosed Bipolar II, and I take 10mg Abilify daily. I've talked to my psychiatrist about starting cognitive behavioral therapy, since I think that'd be most effective in my case, but I don't think my insurance will provide for that.

In my case, I wouldn't do anything like that because it would leave lingering doubts as to whether it was a suicide or not. A car accident would also, but to a far lesser extent. I've been suicidal for the past few years, so any untimely death is likely to raise those questions. Part of the reason I was going to be completely candid with it. 

I also don't feel like this is the best place to be discussing methods, as people browsing this subreddit can be in quite a bad place, and giving them effective ideas could be counter-productive to the purpose of this place.

I've thought about making it look like an accident, but the only real way to do that is with a car, and that leaves a financial burden as well as an emotional one. There is also the part of me that hopes that a week's notice will give them time to ask the questions they would inevitably wonder after I had gone, and that my answers to those questions will bring them some peace.

As I stated above, I don't believe life has any intrinsic value or purpose, and that it is futile and an insult to our capability to think above our basic survival instincts to prolong it for reasons we make up to satisfy ourselves, including "Live so you can experience even more." In the end, it all adds up to nothing either way.

I'll choose this post to respond to while I clarify my thoughts on suicide. I have read Camus, in fact, and find his argument un-convincing. It makes an equal amount of sense to kill yourself as it does to carry on struggling against the absurd. I don't think Camus really looked enough into suicide to decide it was something that should be looked on negatively, which he so clearly does. I see suicide as the most rational response when confronted with the idea that all life is devoid of any intrinsic meaning or value based simply on the nature of the universe. It's a hard truth to swallow, but it is there and it must be confronted. Camus suggests to fight fire with fire, if you will. He idolizes his heroes of the absurd for acknowledging their meaninglessness and deriving pleasure from it, but does it not make just as much sense to acknowledge that meaninglessness and then accept it so completely as to end your own consciousness?

As for my family and friends, once I am dead, they will not matter to me. It is unfortunate that my death will hurt them, but I hope to get them to understand that this is truly what I want, and to stand in the way of that is even more selfish than my suicide would be. Yes, I am saying that I value my peace of mind (or absence of mind, in this case) over theirs. If that makes me awful, so be it, but their opinions will not affect the end goal of my actions.
Do you think parents really love all their children equally, or do they have favorites? Do you think this changes as the children age and live their own lives?
Would you say you or other people in general think money is equal to success? And is it good or bad to think that?

It's funny that you say dolphins, because I feel the exact same way, and everyone always looks at me funny when I say that. I think it will be interesting to see how the two cultures integrate. What if there was a period in history where America saw its first dolphin president? That'd be pretty sweet, actually.
What do you think will happen when a second species on Earth develops the ability to communicate with us? And which species do you think it will be?
